Subject: Post-call follow-up: log TTL, backups & deletion SLAs

Tom / Security team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so you have a single place to reference. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of what we covered
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted service controls (availability, confidentiality, processing integrity). We also have an internal roadmap item to extend some coverage for Dedicated deployments; Laura will include the latest scope notes below.
- Data categories: customer content (app inputs / outputs), logs/telemetry (request metadata, perf traces), backups (encrypted snapshots).
- Retention asks: you asked for an RPO/RTO and whether we can support a 90-day rolling log TTL for application-level logs and a 365-day backup retention for compliance. You also asked about deletion proof and whether backups are included in deletion SLAs.

What Redwood can commit to today (proposal)
1) Active logs (request + app-level telemetry): configurable TTL per-account; default 90 days. We can reduce to 45 days on request for specific accounts where shorter retention is required.
2) Backups/snapshots: default retention 365 days for Hosted; for Dedicated/Private we can align retention to customer policy but will require contractual language.
3) Deletion/erase: we issue a deletion job that removes live data within the SLA window. Backups are immutable snapshots — deletion from backups occurs on the next scheduled backup rotation; we can add an SLA that commits to purging customer data from backup within 30 days of a deletion request, subject to contractual terms and legal hold exceptions.
4) Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary attached, and we can provide redacted backup manifest samples and deletion job run logs for audit purposes.

Attachments included: SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (summary), proposed-deletion-sla-draft.docx (contract language put-forward).

Next steps / ask list (proposed timeline)
- Tom / Security: confirm whether 90-day TTL for logs is acceptable, or if you require default 45 days for this account — reply by EOD Thu (2 business days).
- Redwood (Laura): I’ve asked Laura to share the minimal technical note with the backup rotation cadence and the exact locations that will be included/excluded from deletion. Deliverable by Wed (3 business days).
- Initiate vendor security questionnaire: we’ll push the vendor security questionnaire (xlsx) and follow up on specifics — Tom indicated legal approval might take ~2 weeks.

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute follow-up next week to finalize the SLA language.

Thanks — Mina

Subject: Technical note: backup rotation, log TTL, and deletion job mechanics

Hi Tom / Mina — adding the technical details Mina promised. Summary below plus a short appendix that I’ve attached as an XLS for the questionnaire mapping.

High-level mechanics
- Logs (app/request traces): stored in a tiered Kafka-like store for 0–7 days hot, then compressed cold-tier (object store) for the remainder of the TTL. TTL enforcement is an automated job that deletes keys from the object store and removes indexing entries; for multi-tenant Dedicated deployments we can scope the job per-tenant namespace.
- Backups: encrypted incremental snapshots with full weekly checkpoints. Snapshots are immutable; deletions from backups are implemented by removing snapshot manifests and scheduling a compaction/rewrite process. This process can be paused for legal holds.
- Deletion proof: we can provide a signed deletion manifest (hash list) and a job run log that shows snapshot manifest removal and compaction completion. For Hosted accounts, the compaction window typically completes within 24–30 days after manifest removal; for Dedicated accounts compaction may take up to 45–60 days depending on storage backend and region.

Proposed default values for contract language
- Active log TTL: 90 days (opt-down to 45 days by request).
- Backup retention (hosted): 365 days.
- Deletion-from-backup SLA (hosted): purge scheduled and completed within 30 days from deletion confirmation, excluding legal hold.
- Deletion-from-backup SLA (dedicated/private): purge scheduled within 30 days; completion target 60 days due to compaction window.

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (I filled the first sheet with answers), proposed-deletion-sla-draft.docx (legal language), backup-rotation-appendix.xlsx (technical appendix).

Thanks Mina / Laura — appreciate the clear follow-up and the attachments. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we move to legal: 
1) For the 30-day deletion-from-backup SLA (hosted) — can you clarify whether that is measured from the time of the customer deletion request or from the time Redwood confirms deletion has been queued? We prefer it measured from the confirmation to avoid ambiguity.
2) For Dedicated we need the 60-day completion target to be explicit in the contract; otherwise our compliance team will flag it.
3) We will start the vendor security questionnaire but please treat the answers in the first sheet as preliminary; we may follow-up with more detailed controls questions.

Also: can you provide a sample signed deletion manifest (redacted) so our audit team can see the format? If you can push that to the Drive link in your note, we’ll get legal started.

Next steps from Medverity
- Security: start questionnaire and come back with any follow-ups — aim to have initial pass in 10 business days.
- Legal: review proposed-deletion-sla-draft and circle back with redlines.

If you’re open, let’s lock a 30-minute call next Wed to confirm measurement semantics and finalize the contract path.

Regards,
